chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Ismāʿīl ibn Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, that he said:
Regarding a man who delays the ẓuhr until the time of the ʿaṣr enters, then he begins with the ʿaṣr and then performs the ẓuhr.
So the correct understanding of this report is that when the time of the ʿaṣr has become restricted, he begins with it and then performs the ẓuhr, according to what we have explained in detail.

key_terms.تَضَيَّقَ: became restricted or too narrow in time
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time assigned to the ʿaṣr prayer
key_terms.يُؤَخِّرُ: delays the performance of the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone delays ẓuhr until ʿaṣr time becomes tight, which salat should be performed first?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for one who delays the ẓuhr prayer until the time of ʿaṣr has entered. Its intent is that if the time for ʿaṣr has become tight, one should perform ʿaṣr first and then make up ẓuhr, reflecting the jurisprudential ordering of obligatory salat when time is constrained.
